After push 5, push 3, push 7, push 3, push 1, pop, pop, what does getMin return, and how many elements does the main stack hold?
questions.explanation: Main stack after the pushes: 5 3 7 3 1; auxiliary stack: 5 3 3 3 1. Two pops remove 1 and 3 from the main stack and 1 and 3 from the auxiliary one, leaving main 5 3 7 and auxiliary 5 3 3. getMin reads the auxiliary top, 3, and the main stack has 3 elements.

questions.stem: The non-zero part of a 10 × 10 lower-triangular matrix (entries a[i][j] with j ≤ i, indices from 1) is stored column by column in a one-dimensional array starting at address 2000, with 4 bytes per element. What is the address of a[8][5]?
questions.explanation: Column c of the lower triangle holds rows c to 10, which is 11 − c entries. Columns 1 to 4 hold 10 + 9 + 8 + 7 = 34 entries, the formula (j − 1)n − (j − 1)(j − 2)/2 = 40 − 6. In column 5 the entries a[5][5], a[6][5], a[7][5] precede a[8][5], 3 more. Offset 37, address 2000 + 37 × 4 = 2148. Using the row-major formula i(i − 1)/2 + j − 1 = 32 gives the wrong 2128.

questions.stem: A three-dimensional array A[−1..2][0..4][5..7] of 8-byte elements is stored in row-major order starting at address 1200. What is the address of A[1][3][6]?
questions.explanation: The last two dimensions have n₂ = 5 and n₃ = 3 elements, so each plane holds 15. A[1][3][6] has 1 − (−1) = 2 full planes before it, then 3 − 0 = 3 full rows of 3, then 6 − 5 = 1 element: (2 × 5 + 3) × 3 + 1 = 40 elements. Address 1200 + 40 × 8 = 1520. Ignoring the lower bounds would give (1 × 5 + 3) × 3 + 6 = 30, the wrong 1440.

questions.stem: Evaluate the prefix expression − * 3 + 4 2 / 8 ^ 2 2, where ^ is exponentiation and every operator is binary.
questions.explanation: Scan right to left, pushing operands; at an operator the first value popped is its left operand. 2, 2 → ^ gives 2² = 4 → 8 → / gives 8 / 4 = 2 → 2, 4 → + gives 6 → 3 → * gives 3 × 6 = 18 → − gives 18 − 2 = 16. As an infix expression it is 3 × (4 + 2) − 8 / 2², which is 16. Taking the first pop as the right operand, as in postfix, gives −17.5.

questions.stem: The infix expression a + b * ( c − d / e ) ^ f − g is converted to postfix with the usual operator-stack algorithm (^ highest and right-associative; * and / next; + and − lowest; all others left-associative). Left parentheses are pushed onto the same stack. What is the largest number of symbols (operators and left parentheses) on the stack at any moment?
questions.explanation: + is pushed; * has higher precedence, so it is pushed on +; ( is pushed; − stops at ( and is pushed; / beats −, so it is pushed. The stack now holds + * ( − /, 5 symbols. ) pops / and − and removes (, leaving + *; ^ is pushed (3 symbols); the final − pops ^, * and + and is pushed alone. The output is a b c d e / − f ^ * + g −, and the peak is 5.

questions.stem: A queue is implemented with a circular singly linked list, and only one external pointer P into the list is kept. Where should P point so that both enqueue and dequeue run in O(1) time?
options: To the second node from the front
Nowhere: O(1) for both needs two external pointers
questions.explanation: With P at the rear, the front is P->next. Enqueue: new->next = P->next; P->next = new; P = new. Dequeue: f = P->next; P->next = f->next (P becomes NULL if f was the only node). Both are O(1). With P at the front, enqueue must find the rear, and dequeue must update the rear's next pointer, each an O(n) walk around the ring. The second node has the same problem, and one pointer is enough, so D is false.

pitfalls.text: Array stacks start with top = −1, so the full test is top == N − 1, not top == N; off-by-one here causes both overflow and underflow bugs.
front == rear in a circular queue is ambiguous between empty and full; keep a count or leave one slot unused, and read which convention the question uses.
A function that inserts at the head must take Node ** or return the new head; changing a Node * parameter does not change the caller's head.
A tail pointer makes insertion at the tail O(1) but not deletion: the second-last node of a singly linked list still needs an O(n) walk.
In postfix evaluation the first value popped is the right operand: for a b −, compute a − b, not b − a.
^ is right-associative: an incoming ^ must not pop a ^ already on the operator stack.
Deleting a node without free() leaks memory, and traversing a list that might contain a cycle with while (p != NULL) never ends; use Floyd's check first.

revisionCard.heading: Stacks and queues
lines: Stack LIFO, queue FIFO, deque both ends: all core operations O(1)
Stack permutations of n inputs: Catalan C(2n, n)/(n + 1) = 1, 2, 5, 14, 42
Circular queue, one slot unused: empty front == rear, full (rear + 1) mod N == front
Queue from two stacks: O(1) amortized, O(n) worst for one dequeue
Circular list queue: keep the rear pointer; front is rear->next

revisionCard.heading: Expressions
lines: Operand → output; ( push; ) pop to (; operator pops higher (and equal if left-assoc)
^ right-assoc: A ^ B ^ C → A B C ^ ^
Postfix eval: pop b then a, push a op b
Prefix eval: scan right to left, first pop is the left operand

Floyd: slow 1, fast 2; reset one to head to find the loop start
Middle: while (fast && fast->next) stops slow at ⌊n/2⌋ (second middle for even n)

Doubling dynamic array: append O(1) amortized

errata.claim: Infix to postfix: on reading an operator, pop all operators of higher or equal precedence to the output, then push it.
errata.correction: Popping on equal precedence is right only for left-associative operators. For the right-associative ^, an incoming ^ pops only operators of strictly higher precedence, so A ^ B ^ C becomes A B C ^ ^; the stated rule gives A B ^ C ^, which means (A ^ B) ^ C. Popping must also stop at a ( on the stack.
